description:
fz-go4.18.12 finding 4. Each callee return-type revision triggers a FULL re-inference of every caller body: AnalyzeActivation(main) fired 22x on 00001 (12 distinct analyses, 10 no-change); callsite.defined 133 fires / 26 keys with 76 byte-identical re-publications; return_type.defined 45 fires / only 8 changed on 00181. FIX direction (design work): batch callee revisions before re-analyzing a caller, and/or granularize analysis so only the affected callsite's contribution is recomputed; at minimum suppress identical re-publications (interacts with T1's stop-at-unchanged). ACCEPTANCE: identical callsite/return_type re-publications ~0 on the corpus; AnalyzeActivation fire counts justified by distinct input revisions.

RE-MEASURED 2026-07-02 at e55c8e185 (diagnose-only pass, no code change): counts are UNCHANGED from the original measurement -- AnalyzeActivation(main) still 22 fires / 12 distinct / 10 no-change; callsite.defined still 133/26/76, exact match on all three digits. The re-scope hypothesis ("much of this is downstream of the .18.22 oscillation/wipes") does NOT hold for this specific finding -- .18.22 and the subsequent census/keystone arc (.28.1/.28.7/.28.8) did not touch this mechanism.

DIAGNOSIS: suppression is already correctly implemented -- world.rs's define_callsite_summary/define_activation_return/define_activation_analysis each compute an authoritative changed bool and jobs/semantic.rs::analyze_activation only bumps a revision (driving downstream wake) when changed is true; a byte-identical re-run does NOT propagate a spurious wake further. The remaining churn is a genuine CROSS-ROUND BATCHING GAP, not a suppression gap: AnalyzeActivation(main)'s 22 enqueues are each triggered by a SEPARATE single-fact revision bump from a different callee across sequential ascent rounds (one step bumps DispatchMask(FunctionId(33)), the next separately bumps ReturnType(FunctionId(33)), each independently re-enqueuing main's analysis). The scheduler already coalesces multiple simultaneous wakes for the SAME job within one applied step (scheduler.rs coalesced_seen/enqueue_step) -- but main's callees settle across many sequential rounds, so there's nothing to coalesce within any single step. This is the expected behavior of a monotone-ascent per-revision wake model (the correct northstar pull shape, NOT a follow_up push) when nothing yet detects "this callee's revision stream has settled, stop re-running dependents until the whole cone is done."

WHY NOT FIXED HERE: closing this gap needs either (a) SCC/round-settledness-gated re-analysis mirroring fz-go4.18.22's proven RuntimeDemand pattern (bottom-start monotone ascent settling a whole SCC before publishing to dependents outside it), or (b) granularizing analyze_activation so one callee's revision only recomputes the affected call site's contribution instead of re-walking the whole body -- both are real incremental-analysis redesigns, not a one-line fix, and both would touch the same enqueue/wake paths fz-go4.18.24's follow_up migration is actively converting -- sequence after .18.24 to avoid concurrent churn on the same files.

MEASUREMENT GAP NOTED: return_type.defined telemetry (unlike callsite.defined) carries no explicit `changed` boolean, only (root_id, function_id, ascents, rebased) -- the original "45 fires / 8 changed" split can't be independently re-verified without a noisy Ty-id-churn proxy (interned ids shift across ascent rounds even for structurally-equivalent types). Cheap ride-along for whoever picks this up: add a `changed: bool` field to return_type.defined telemetry matching callsite.defined's existing field.

ACCEPTANCE (unchanged): identical callsite/return_type re-publications ~0 on the corpus; AnalyzeActivation fire counts justified by distinct input revisions. Superseded by a properly-scoped design ticket -- see fz-go4.18.31.

comments.text: Re-scoped context: much of the re-analysis churn is downstream of the .18.22 oscillation/wipes. Re-measure the AnalyzeActivation/callsite re-publication counts after .18.22 lands; implement only what remains.

title: Per-callee-revision whole-caller re-analysis: batch/granularize activation re-inference
